title: Predictive SLA Allocation & GPU Class Recommendation for Dedicated Reservations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Design a predictive SLA allocation and GPU-class recommendation component to be integrated into the Dedicated Capacity intake flow. The goal is to reduce manual sizing back-and-forth with enterprise customers by auto-suggesting: (1) an SLA band (latency/availability targets), (2) reserved throughput (tokens/sec or qps), and (3) preferred GPU class and burst policy. This should incorporate historical usage signals, workload shape (inference vs. batch), and customer risk profile.

Motivation / Problem:
- Sales and Solutions teams report >4 touchpoints and ~10 days on average to finalize reservation sizing for enterprise customers.
- Mismatched GPU class choices and overly conservative SLAs increase cost by 20–40% for customers and lead to suboptimal pool utilization for Redwood.
- Current intake form relies on self-reported peak qps and a static sizing table; no predictive guardrails or automated fallback recommendations exist.

Success criteria / acceptance criteria:
- Prototype recommendation appears in intake UI and provides: SLA band suggestion (S1/S2/S3), reserved throughput number, GPU class ranking (e.g., A100-80GB, H100-80GB, T4-ext), and recommended burst credit amount.
- Recommendations are justified with an explainability note listing the top 3 signals used (e.g., historical qps, 95th pct token length, concurrency pattern).
- Piloted with 3 enterprise customers; at least one customer accepts recommendation without changes.
- Backend exposes an endpoint for ENG to consume (docs + sample payload), integrated with intake flow.

Proposed approach:
1) Data model and signals (ENG + Data):
   - Historical API telemetry (qps, p95 latency, token distributions) from last 90 days.
   - Customer SLA tiering from contract metadata and legal constraints.
   - Workload profile: chat vs. single-turn, average context length, long-tail spike frequency.
   - Business risk tags (regulated, PII, high-sensitivity) from account metadata.

2) Heuristic + ML hybrid recommender:
   - Start with deterministic heuristics that map 95th p99 qps -> base reserved throughput and apply headroom factor based on spike cadence.
   - Add a lightweight gradient-boosted model (explainable) to re-rank GPU class based on sequence length distribution and expected memory/KV cache pressure.
   - Fallback to conservative defaults for accounts with limited telemetry.

3) Scaling and burst policies:
   - Recommend a warm pool size (N preprovisioned replicas), burst credit (token/sec * burst_multiplier), and preemption tolerance level (preemptible vs. non-preemptible).
   - Suggest autoscaling thresholds (scale-up at 70% reserved utilization predicted for 3 consecutive minutes; scale-down after sustained 10 minutes below 40%).

Trade-offs discussed:
- Aggressive recommendations reduce cost but increase risk of SLA misses; we will surface trade-off sliders in the UI (Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive) for SRE/Account to pick.
- ML model complexity vs. explainability: choose a small GBDT to maintain interpretability and avoid opaque deep-learning-based estimators for first release.
- Pre-warming vs. burst capacity: pre-warm increases steady cost, burst risks throttling. Default to hybrid (small warm pool + burst credit) for chat-heavy workloads.

Progress log / decisions (chronological):
- 2025-02-11 (Aisha Patel) — Ticket created. Linked initial intake survey and stakeholder list.
- 2025-02-13 (Marcus Li) — Scoping meeting with Metrics and Serving Runtime. Agreed to use 90-day telemetry as primary signal. Action: ENG to extract sample CSV and define telemetry schema.
- 2025-02-15 (Nina Gomez, Data Eng) — Delivered sample telemetry extract: s3://redwood-data/dedicated/intake-sample-90d.csv. Added to ticket comments.
- 2025-02-18 (Marcus Li) — Proposal: deterministic heuristic + lightweight model. Requested estimate from ENG (see dependencies ENG-21045).
- 2025-02-20 (Jason Park, Solutions Eng) — Field feedback from sales: customers prefer explicit cost delta estimates for each recommendation. Added to acceptance criteria.
- 2025-02-22 (Design review, Leila Morgan) — Wireframe for UI card approved (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DC/Predictive+SLA+Draft). Design asked for an explainability tooltip and a manual override CTA.
- 2025-02-24 (Security review kick-off, Priya Shah) — Confirmed no new PII required; security review not blocking.
- 2025-02-26 (Marcus Li) — Marking ticket Planned. ENG to scope API and warm-pool instrumentation (ENG-22299).

Open questions / blockers:
- Which telemetry retention window is authoritative for low-volume customers? (Data suggests 90d is ok but Sales asked for 12 months for regulated customers.)
- Finalize mapping matrix between GPU families and expected per-token cost across our cloud partners (cost modeling required).
- How to present cost-vs-reliability trade-offs in a simple way for non-technical procurement contacts.

Next steps / immediate actions:
- ENG (Marcus Wu) to provide API contract and sample payload by 2025-03-03 (dependency ENG-22299).
- Data Eng (Nina) to run 1 week of backtests for recommendation accuracy and produce a confusion matrix for GPU selection by 2025-03-07.
- Product to schedule pilot with two existing enterprise customers: Acero Health and NimbusSearch; finalize pilot scope by 2025-03-10.

Notes for rollout and monitoring:
- Add telemetry to track: recommendation acceptance rate, post-deployment SLA breaches per customer, actual vs. predicted reserved utilization.
- Define rollback policy: if pilot customers see >1 SLA miss attributable to recommendation, revert to manual sizing and open incident review.

If you are reviewing: please comment on the proposed autoscaling thresholds and whether the 90-day telemetry window fits your product/regulatory expectations.
